intuition.title: Core growth and assembly are different procedures
intuition.text: The two metal preparations differ in solvent and ligand timing: Au uses toluene and dodecanethiol after reduction, while Ag uses chloroform and dodecanethiol before borohydride. Film conditions use preformed particles; they do not establish new independent core-synthesis batches.

intuition.title: Superlattice packing is not atomic crystal phase
intuition.text: The detailed results identify fcc packing of nanocrystals and a (111)s plane parallel to the substrate. The summary instead says normal; the discrepancy is retained. Atomic Au/Ag phase, lattice parameters and coordinates are not supplied by these SEM observations.

intuition.title: Solvent and sonication select different assemblies
intuition.text: Au hexane gives rough mounds, whereas chloroform gives relatively smooth films with triangular step-growth features. The 9:1 hexane/ethanol mixture gives dendritic, nonordered deposits without sonication and faceted superlattice crystallites with sonication during casting. Sonication of good-solvent hexane/toluene dispersions did not produce homogeneous superlattice nucleation.

intuition.title: Temperature affects film morphology, not a reported new core size
intuition.text: Au films from toluene have mounds at room temperature and become flatter but locally disordered at 40°C. Many more defects than in room-temperature chloroform films remain. No new particle size is assigned to this temperature comparison.

intuition.title: Surface diffusion interpretation is model-scoped
intuition.text: The authors discuss bulk diffusion, adsorption, surface diffusion and incorporation or desorption. More attractive interactions and larger supersaturation favor short surface diffusion and radial mound growth; lower supersaturation and longer diffusion favor step growth. The roughly ten-diameter or60nm diffusion scale is an estimate, not measured core or mound size.

intuition.title: SI optical results do not create structural specimens
intuition.text: The SI follows separately prepared Au dispersions in two solvents using absorbance. Final concentrations, elapsed times and fractional losses stay with their optical experiments. Their particle size and exact link to a main-film specimen are unknown. Small short-time changes are interpreted by the authors as insufficient to explain the main solvent-dependent film differences.

general_background.title: Thermodynamics and kinetics
general_background.summary: Thermodynamics describes which states are energetically favoured, while kinetics governs how quickly a system can move between them. A change can be favourable yet proceed slowly when an activation barrier or limited transport restricts the pathway.
